inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,998 normalized lines of Motohashi's article. The prose supports a complete conceptual chain from a Gaussian-smoothed fourth moment, through additive divisor and Kloosterman-sum transforms, Kuznetsov/Petersson spectral separation, global meromorphic continuation, specialization, and saddle-point extraction of the asymptotic spectral formula. The PDF text layer frequently damages displayed formulas, so units preserve prose-supported mechanisms and equation-local context while flagging exact constants, signs, kernels, and parameter placements for verification against the retained scan. No v1 units were assigned.

sections_inspected.label: Title and publication front matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies the article and author; no mathematical unit selected.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction and statement of results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates the fourth-moment analogue of Atkinson's formula, sets up automorphic spectral data, states the explicit formula and corollary, and compares alternate routes.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Reduction to sums of Kloosterman sums
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Embeds the moment in a four-variable meromorphic family, separates shifted divisor variables through Ramanujan sums and Mellin inversion, and derives Kloosterman-sum kernels.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Spectral expansion
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Applies corrected Kuznetsov trace formulas and the Kloosterman zeta spectral decomposition to separate variables into continuous, Maass, and holomorphic spectral contributions.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Analytic continuation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reduces continuation to one Mellin-Barnes kernel, proves its global meromorphy and decay, and continues the continuous spectrum by contour shifting.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Specialization
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Specializes the four-variable identity at the fourth-moment point, regularizes the main term by cancellation, bounds residual contour pieces, and identifies the hypergeometric kernel.

sections_inspected.label: 6. Asymptotics
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Obtains uniform spectral-kernel bounds, localizes the relevant Maass range, performs the saddle-point calculation, and assembles the asymptotic corollary.

sections_inspected.label: References and author back matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic and publication metadata; no mathematical unit selected.

accepted_units.title: From Atkinson's diagonal split to automorphic spectral decomposition
accepted_units.why_material: Explains the reusable strategic replacement: a diagonal/off-diagonal split that Poisson summation handles for a double sum becomes a determinant split of matrix-indexed quadruple sums, with the SL(2,Z) spectral decomposition replacing Poisson summation. It also previews the full proof pipeline and its analytic-continuation bottleneck.
accepted_units.context_note: Keep the full prose from the Atkinson comparison through the pipeline preview; the extracted displays (1.1), (1.3)-(1.5) are damaged but their roles are stated in surrounding prose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the conceptual bridge is prose-recoverable, but exact displayed decompositions and the smoothed moment definition require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Maass spectrum, Hecke coefficients, and multiplicative L-function factorization
accepted_units.why_material: Collects the non-holomorphic spectral objects later used to turn Kloosterman sums into separated variables: Laplace eigenvalues, parity, Hecke eigenvalues, Fourier normalization, spectral weights, Hecke L-functions, coefficient bounds, the divisor-twist factorization, functional equation, and polynomial growth.
accepted_units.context_note: The definitions are mutually dependent and should remain together because later formulas use all of the notation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for exact normalizations and gamma factors: prose and equation labels establish the structure, but formulas (1.6)-(1.11) should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Holomorphic cusp-form counterpart of the Maass spectral data
accepted_units.why_material: Builds the holomorphic branch parallel to the Maass branch: Petersson bases, Hecke eigenvalues and L-series, divisor-twist factorization, analytic continuation, growth, Fourier weights, and the aggregate weight bound later needed for absolute convergence.
accepted_units.context_note: Retain the whole setup because its point is the structural parallel with the preceding Maass construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact Petersson/Hecke normalizations and (1.12)-(1.15) are formula-sensitive and need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Explicit fourth-moment formula as a three-part spectral expansion
accepted_units.why_material: States that the Gaussian-smoothed fourth moment decomposes into an explicit main term, a continuous spectral integral, a Maass discrete sum, and a holomorphic cusp-form sum, and explains why every spectral expression converges absolutely and why the Gaussian weight is operationally preferred.
accepted_units.context_note: Use the theorem only at the structural level unless the scan is consulted; the text extraction severely damages the displayed formula and kernel.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: coefficients, arguments, signs, and the hypergeometric kernel in (1.16) are not safely recoverable from text alone; retained scan verification is mandatory for exact use.

accepted_units.title: Mean-square analogy, Voronoi transformation, and the missing spectral analogue
accepted_units.why_material: Compares the fourth-moment spectral formula with an explicit mean-square formula, explains how Voronoi summation recovers Atkinson's result, identifies the absence of a comparable transform for spectral sums as a genuine obstruction, and motivates asymptotic evaluation as an alternate route.
accepted_units.context_note: The mechanism and obstruction are explicit in prose; the displayed mean-square and saddle formulas are supporting evidence rather than safe exact data.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium to high: the comparison is prose-stable, while formulas (1.17)-(1.18) require scan verification for exact terms.

accepted_units.title: Asymptotic spectral wave formula and its conceptual interpretation
accepted_units.why_material: States the simplified asymptotic regime, interprets fourth-moment values as coupled to the full non-Euclidean Laplace spectrum, and distinguishes the method from a prior smoothing/reflection route that does not preserve full explicitness.
accepted_units.context_note: The spectral-wave interpretation and method comparison are reliable prose; the exact corollary display is degraded.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for the exact asymptotic formula and range; low for the source's stated interpretation and independence claim.

accepted_units.title: Four-variable meromorphic family encoding the smoothed moment
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces a four-complex-variable zeta integral, recovers the target moment at a special point after explicit residue terms, expands it into a quadruple Dirichlet sum, and splits it into diagonal and two off-diagonal pieces. This is the central deformation that makes later continuation possible.
accepted_units.context_note: Keep the continuation-to-D-minus discussion with the decomposition because it explains both recovery of the target and why a second continuation is needed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the roles of Y, Y0, and Y1 are clear, but the exact integral, residue correction, special point, and zeta quotient need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Additive-character and Mellin separation of the shifted divisor correlation
accepted_units.why_material: Rejects an insufficiently explicit appeal to general Eisenstein convolution theory, expands a divisor sum through Ramanujan additive characters, then Mellin-inverts the smooth weight to separate the remaining variables. It also records meromorphy and rapid vertical decay of the Mellin transform and the functional equation of the additive-twist Dirichlet series.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit includes the explicitness motivation, both separation steps, and the analytic properties that justify them.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for formulas (2.6)-(2.13); the source prose safely supports the transformation sequence and convergence claims.

accepted_units.title: Contour shift converts additive twists into Kloosterman-sum kernels
accepted_units.why_material: Defines an overlapping domain where the Mellin contour may be shifted, extracts pole residues, applies the additive-twist functional equation, and reorganizes the remainder into positive- and negative-sign Kloosterman sums. Lemma 1 packages the result and shows only trivial Kloosterman bounds are needed at this stage.
accepted_units.context_note: The domain restrictions, residue terms, kernel definitions, and convergence statement form one coherent reduction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high for the displayed kernels and factors in (2.14)-(2.23); scan verification is required before exact symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Twisted diagonal decomposition as a completion of van der Corput's method
accepted_units.why_material: Records an alternate derivation: twist the diagonal/off-diagonal split by coprime parameters, average with weights while exploiting invariance of the left side, and obtain Kloosterman sums for smooth inputs. The source presents this as a general route to exponential-sum bounds using SL(2,Z) theory.
accepted_units.context_note: This short digression is self-contained and conceptually distinct from the Ramanujan-sum derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low to medium: the prose gives the method; the single extracted decomposition is damaged but not needed to retain the conceptual move.

accepted_units.title: Corrected opposite-sign Kuznetsov trace formula via K-Bessel inversion
accepted_units.why_material: States the trace formula for opposite-sign Kloosterman sums, flags corrections to earlier statements, and sketches its proof by changing the Poincare-series inner product and using Kontorovich-Lebedev inversion. This is the mechanism that produces Maass and continuous spectra for the negative-sign kernel.
accepted_units.context_note: Retain hypotheses on the test function and the proof sketch; correctness of the exact normalization cannot be inferred from OCR.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the sign, constants, Bessel transform, spectral weights, and integrand in (3.3)-(3.4) require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Rapid-decay transform and spectral expansion of the negative-sign kernel
accepted_units.why_material: Applies the corrected trace formula to the constructed kernel, computes its Bessel transform, proves rapid decay uniformly on compact parameter sets by contour deformation and Stirling estimates, and uses Hecke factorization to obtain Lemma 3's separated continuous and Maass contributions.
accepted_units.context_note: The decay argument is essential context because it justifies every exchange of sums and integrals.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the detailed transforms and spectral products in (3.5)-(3.12) are formula-damaged; only the proof architecture is safe without the scan.

accepted_units.title: Kloosterman-sum zeta function exposes Maass, holomorphic, continuous, and diagonal terms
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces the Kloosterman-sum zeta function and its four-part Kuznetsov expansion, proves convergence in an enlarged half-plane, and invokes Petersson's identity to identify the holomorphic spectral weights and derive their aggregate bound.
accepted_units.context_note: The convergence argument and Petersson comparison should remain with the decomposition because they certify the holomorphic branch.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: exact half-planes, gamma factors, Bessel series, signs, and normalization in (3.13)-(3.20) need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Positive-sign kernel expansion and cancellation of the diagonal auxiliary term
accepted_units.why_material: Mellin-inverts the positive-sign Kloosterman kernel against the zeta-function spectral decomposition, obtains Maass, continuous, holomorphic, and diagonal pieces, proves rapid decay permitting reordering, and shows an auxiliary diagonal series telescopes/cancels before reassembly.
accepted_units.context_note: The cancellation is inseparable from the positive-sign decomposition because it explains why the final spectral formula has only three contributions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: formulas (3.21)-(3.32) are heavily degraded and require the scan for exact coefficients and signs.

accepted_units.title: Lemma 5 assembles the full positive-sign spectral expansion
accepted_units.why_material: Combines the positive-sign kernel calculation with Hecke identities to give continuous, Maass, and holomorphic separated-variable contributions and defines generalized Mellin-Barnes kernels suitable for continuation beyond the initial domain.
accepted_units.context_note: This closes the restricted-domain spectral stage and directly sets up the continuation problem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: all exact spectral L-function arguments and kernel normalizations in (3.33)-(3.37) require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Reduce all kernel continuation to one Mellin-Barnes function
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that the previously distinct Bessel/spectral kernels are algebraic combinations of a single Mellin-Barnes function, defines the exceptional hyperplane set, and uses path deformation on its connected complement to establish single-valued regular continuation there.
accepted_units.context_note: Keep the exceptional-set construction because it controls when separating contours exist.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the reduction relations (4.1)-(4.3) and precise exceptional hyperplanes require scan verification, though the analytic strategy is prose-clear.

accepted_units.title: Hypergeometric residue extraction gives global meromorphy and rapid decay
accepted_units.why_material: Converts the Mellin-Barnes kernel into a hypergeometric integral, expands it into finitely many explicit residues plus a controlled remainder, and lets the number of extracted poles grow to continue the kernel over all five variables. Lemma 6 adds rapid decay, which then propagates to the discrete spectral series.
accepted_units.context_note: The finite-residue-plus-remainder construction is the essential proof; omitted routine decay details are adequately bounded by the lemma statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high for (4.5)-(4.9), residue coefficients, and exceptional loci; the scan is needed for exact reconstruction.

accepted_units.title: Contour shifting across arithmetic poles completes global continuation
accepted_units.why_material: Combines the two continuous-spectrum integrals, rewrites them using the master kernel, shifts the spectral contour, accounts separately for parameter poles and poles indexed by zeta zeros, and uses an arbitrarily wide bounded-parameter box to prove global meromorphy of the off-diagonal family.
accepted_units.context_note: The occurrence of zeta-zero-indexed residues is part of the continuation mechanism, not evidence about zero locations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: pole lists and residue formulas (4.12)-(4.16) are OCR-sensitive; scan verification is mandatory for exact use.

accepted_units.title: Specialize the continued family and isolate regular spectral contributions
accepted_units.why_material: Specializes the global decomposition at the fourth-moment point, proves that discrete spectral kernels may be evaluated there without modification, cancels odd Maass parity through the functional equation, moves the continuous contour back to the imaginary axis, and separates polar main terms from a regular integral.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit bridges abstract continuation and the explicit formula; retain both the local regularity argument and the symmetric P_T/P_-T reassembly.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: special-point coordinates, parity factors, and equations (5.1)-(5.7) require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Regular main term recovered from cancellation of eleven meromorphic pieces
accepted_units.why_material: Computes polar contributions, rewrites the main term as eleven explicit meromorphic summands, and extracts its finite value by perturbing along a generic direction so individual Laurent singularities avoid collision while their aggregate singular parts cancel.
accepted_units.context_note: The generic-direction device is a reusable regularization move; exact summand formulas are retained only as scan-dependent context.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the eleven terms and their Laurent coefficients are not reliably recoverable from the extracted formulas.

accepted_units.title: Split a singular kernel into its residue and a regular contour remainder
accepted_units.why_material: Handles the difficult main-term component by moving a contour across one pole, separating an explicit residue that has the desired derivative-integral form, and bounding the regular remainder after a second contour shift with Stirling estimates and Cauchy's formula. Parallel pieces then inherit the same control.
accepted_units.context_note: The source's prose safely establishes the two-stage contour strategy and error scale; formulas are needed only for exact constants.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the extracted residue, four contour pieces, and bounds (5.10)-(5.13) need scan verification for exact parameters.

accepted_units.title: Hypergeometric representation closes the explicit-formula proof
accepted_units.why_material: Relates the continued spectral kernels back to the hypergeometric integral at the specialization point and uses the same representation at imaginary and integral spectral parameters to identify the Maass, continuous, and holomorphic kernels in the theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the closure step linking the analytic continuation machinery to the theorem's stated kernel.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: equations (5.14)-(5.15) and the final variable change require the scan before exact symbolic reproduction.

accepted_units.title: Suppress the holomorphic range and establish uniform real-spectral kernel bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Begins asymptotic analysis by deriving rapid decay for integral spectral parameters, sharpens the Mellin-transform bound with exponential dependence on the imaginary coordinate, and shifts contours to obtain uniform decay when the real spectral parameter exceeds the T scale.
accepted_units.context_note: Keep the Gaussian-width assumptions with these bounds because they delimit their uniformity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the qualitative estimates and contour move are prose-clear, but exponents and parameter thresholds in (6.1)-(6.6) require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Complex path deformation localizes the moderate spectral range
accepted_units.why_material: For moderate real spectral parameters, deforms the hypergeometric integral onto a short segment plus a tilted ray, obtains exponential damping on both pieces, and combines this with the large-parameter estimate to restrict the spectral analysis to a finite T-dependent window.
accepted_units.context_note: The line-range cutoff is part of a chain of sufficient estimates rather than a statement that discarded spectrum is absent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact contours and decay exponents in (6.8)-(6.11) require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Eliminate small and positive spectral parameters before saddle analysis
accepted_units.why_material: Reexpresses the kernel as an outer beta-type integral and an inner oscillatory integral, treats very small parameters by splitting and integration by parts, treats positive parameters by contour rotation, and isolates a negative spectral regime where a saddle contributes.
accepted_units.context_note: The stronger assumption on the smoothing width is explicitly presented as a simplification, not a fundamental limit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact logarithmic powers and range endpoints in (6.12)-(6.17) require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Uniform saddle extraction for the negative Maass range
accepted_units.why_material: Locates the saddle, deforms the inner contour into negligible tails plus a steepest-descent segment, proves uniform truncation and Taylor control including the Gaussian weight, evaluates the resulting Gaussian, and applies a second saddle computation to the outer integral to obtain the oscillatory kernel with explicit damping.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a conceptual plan for the two-level saddle method; exact phase, amplitude, and error in (6.18)-(6.26) are scan-dependent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: the text layer damages several contour parametrizations and displayed phases, so the retained scan is required for any exact asymptotic formula.

accepted_units.title: Assemble the corollary from spectral truncation and mean-value control
accepted_units.why_material: Uses rapid decay to discard the holomorphic spectrum, inserts the saddle asymptotic into the surviving negative Maass range, controls the error by a spectral mean value for Hecke L-functions, and shows the continuous spectrum is negligible using classical zeta bounds, thereby proving the announced corollary.
accepted_units.context_note: The cited external estimates are invoked rather than reproved; this unit records their logical role in the assembly.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high for the exact spectral window, oscillatory phase, and error exponent in (6.27); scan and cited-result verification are needed for exact reuse.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Atkinson-to-Kuznetsov replacement principle
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source develops a reusable escalation pattern: deform a moment into a multi-variable Dirichlet family, split diagonal from off-diagonal structure, replace Poisson/Voronoi separation by additive characters and Kloosterman sums, and then replace the classical transform by automorphic spectral decomposition.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a within-source strategic synthesis; it does not assert that every higher moment admits the same deformation or trace formula.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Dual Kloosterman signs generate complementary spectral branches
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The negative-sign and positive-sign Kloosterman kernels require different spectral tools and together produce the continuous, Maass, and holomorphic branches of the fourth-moment formula, with a diagonal auxiliary contribution cancelled before final assembly.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Exact sign conventions and normalizations are text-layer unsafe and must be checked against the scan.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Continuation by a master kernel plus controlled residue bookkeeping
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Instead of continuing each spectral expression separately, the source reduces them to one Mellin-Barnes kernel, proves that kernel globally meromorphic by finite residue extraction and a tunable remainder, then continues the continuous spectrum by contour shifts whose crossed poles are explicitly accounted for before specialization.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The synthesis records the analytic architecture, not the exact pole hyperplanes or residue coefficients.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Regular values emerge from cancellation before specialization
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The explicit fourth-moment identity is recovered by first proving global continuation, then approaching the target along a generic perturbation so singular Laurent pieces cancel in aggregate, while genuinely regular spectral kernels can be specialized directly and the difficult remainder is bounded after pole extraction.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This does not license termwise specialization outside the regularity statements proved in the source.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Spectral localization precedes saddle extraction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The asymptotic proof first removes holomorphic, large, small, and positive spectral ranges by uniform contour estimates, leaving a negative Maass window in which a two-stage saddle calculation yields the oscillatory main contribution; a spectral mean-value estimate then controls aggregation error.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The localized ranges depend on sufficient smoothing hypotheses chosen partly for simplicity and are not claimed optimal.

within_source_saturation: Saturated for prose-supported semantic depth: every usable mathematical section was inspected and its distinct mechanisms are represented in 27 units. Further splitting would mostly isolate formula-only fragments whose exact content is unsafe in this extraction, routine contour/Stirling algebra already subordinate to a represented mechanism, repeated page headers, or bibliography.
stop_reason: Stopped only after covering lines 1-1998 exactly and representing the article's complete source-specific chain: fourth-moment deformation, Kloosterman reduction, dual spectral expansions, master-kernel continuation, specialization/regularization, and asymptotic saddle assembly. Remaining lines are transitions, acknowledgements, references, or formula-level detail requiring scan verification rather than additional standalone semantic units.
